reasoning_trace.value: The paper includes several figures, including Figure 1, which shows the schematic diagram of the proposed photonics-assisted MMW multiband ISAC system. Figure 2 illustrates the block diagram of multiband data fusion processing. Figure 3 displays the measured optical spectra of two OFC tones at the outputs of interleaver. Figure 4 shows the measured optical spectra at the outputs of OC1, OBPF1, and OBPF2. Figure 5 presents the measured spectrum and spectrogram of the generated MMW ISAC signal for both Ka-band and V-band cases. Figure 6 shows the temporal waveforms of the traditional OFDM signal, Ka-band ISAC signal, and V-band ISAC signal. Figure 7 demonstrates the measured BER performances as a function of the received optical powers for the Ka-band and V-band communication demonstrations. Figure 8 displays the photograph of two static metal targets for radar ranging and the obtained radar ranging results. Figure 9 shows the normalized temporal waveforms of radar de-chirped signals before and after dual-band data fusion processing. Figure 10 presents the photograph of two static metal targets separated at 8.5 mm intervals and the obtained range profile results by two single radars and multiband data fusion processing. Figure 11 displays the photograph of the dynamic triangular reflectors mounted on a rotating platform for ultra-high resolution radar imaging and the ISAR imaging results constructed by a single Ka-band radar, a single V-band radar, and multiband data fusion processing. Figure 12 shows the measured BERs of the demodulated OFDM signals and SNRs of the de-chirped radar signals versus different phase modulation indexes of the transmit IF-ISAC signals in the Ka-band and V-band cases. Figure 13 presents the obtained electrical spectrum and spectrogram of the MMW four-band signals generated by the ISAC system covering U, V, and W-bands.

reasoning_trace.description: Explain the System Mechanism and ISAC Coupling Mode found.
reasoning_trace.value: The proposed system is a photonics-assisted MMW multiband ISAC system, which uses a single photonic MMW frequency upconverter to simultaneously generate MMW multiband ISAC signals. The system mechanism involves the use of an optical frequency comb, a wavelength selective switch, an I/Q Mach-Zehnder modulator, and a high-speed photodetector to generate the MMW multiband ISAC signals. The ISAC coupling mode is based on the phase modulation of LFM carriers with different IBWs using the baseband real-valued OFDM signal carried with different bit data, facilitating the high power-efficient radar and communication functions towards multiband/multiuser scenarios.

reasoning_trace.description: Validate the physical consistency of reported metrics (Rate/Resolution).
reasoning_trace.value: The reported metrics, such as the communication data rate of 16 Gbit/s and the two-dimension radar imaging with a range resolution below 3.75 cm, are physically consistent with the system mechanism and ISAC coupling mode. The ultra-high resolution radar ranging and imaging with an 8.6 mm level range resolution are also consistent with the system's capability for multiband data fusion processing.

reasoning_trace.description: Identify the solved problems and remaining open challenges.
reasoning_trace.value: The proposed system solves the problem of achieving large-capacity wireless communication and high-resolution sensing capabilities in a multiband ISAC system. However, the system's performance trade-off between radar and communication functions, as well as the prolongable ability to higher frequencies and more sub-bands integrated functions, are remaining open challenges that need to be addressed in future research.
